summary: 11 datasets investigated. Primary acquisition and decision B (CONDITIONALLY APPROVED) = SymbiPredict (SDPD). Supplementary: Columbia KB (alternative, license pending) and kaushil268 mirror (same family, undocumented).

candidates.name: SymbiPredict (SDPD)
candidates.source: Mendeley Data - dataset (DOI, 2024); documented in peer-reviewed MDPI Electronics paper
candidates.one_line: 41-class / 132-symptom binary symptom-disease matrix, 121 instances per class; symptoms from medical literature, clinical observations, expert consensus; cited in peer-reviewed work.
candidates.format: binary matrix: 132 symptom columns (0/1) + prognosis target
candidates.verdict: B. CONDITIONALLY APPROVED - MANUAL REVIEW REQUIRED (primary)
candidates.notes: Measured: mean MI 0.178 (vs 0.016 current, ~10.8x), avg cosine separability 0.107 (vs 0.694), MI>0.01 in 131/132 features. 94% duplicate rows (association-format redundancy) - Phase 7H must decide representation/deduplication. 3 synonym mappings need manual confirmation.

candidates.name: Columbia University Disease-Symptom Knowledge Database
candidates.source: Columbia DBMI (Prof. Carol Friedman), derived from 25,074 NYP discharge summaries via MedLEE NLP; AMIA 2008 paper PMC2656103
candidates.license: UNKNOWN - no explicit license (manual review required)
candidates.one_line: Real clinical knowledge base: 134 diseases, 401 UMLS-coded symptoms, 1,858 associations with counts from real hospital notes.
candidates.verdict: ALTERNATIVE - CONDITIONALLY APPROVED, license manual review required; real-clinical provenance but association format + unclear license
candidates.notes: Strongest provenance (actual patient records, UMLS codes, ~90% recall / ~92% precision). Association-count format (3-28 assoc per disease) requires weighting/scoring adaptation. 33/401 symptoms exact-match current vocabulary; ~250 unmapped; ~10 non-symptom at high threshold.

candidates.name: Kaushil268 - Disease Prediction using Machine Learning (Kaggle)
candidates.source: Kaggle dataset 'Disease Prediction Using Machine Learning' (kaushil268); downloaded via public GitHub raw mirror of the archive; Apache 2.0
candidates.one_line: Undocumented mirror/derivative of the same 41-class / 131-symptom family already covered by SymbiPredict; long-format with missing cells.
candidates.verdict: REJECTED as materially-better candidate - redundant with documented SymbiPredict; retained as cross-check
candidates.notes: 93.8% duplicate rows, 304 unique vector patterns (synthetic-expression concern). Same disease family as SymbiPredict; prefer the documented, licensed, peer-reviewed version.

candidates.name: Al Shafi et al. (Mendeley rjgjh8hgrt)
candidates.verdict: Reference-only: 85 rows, one per disease; useful symptom list, insufficient training samples.

candidates.name: Mendeley synthetic (2cxccsxydc/1)
candidates.verdict: Explicitly synthetic; does not resolve the synthetic-data concern.

candidates.name: Milton, Yuan, rjanice, PedroAcacia, dianap8, sublimation (Kaggle)
candidates.verdict: Publicly available mirrors/derivations of the same community disease-symptom family (generally 41-class or 24-class with incomplete provenance / no indexed citation). Redundant with SymbiPredict.

candidates.name: Macgyver'milton_dataset - Disease Prediction
candidates.verdict: Small (~4k rows), undocumented derivation of the same family.

candidates.name: Kundan Bedmutha Disease-Symptoms
candidates.verdict: Same community family; no independent citation.

candidates.name: Zenodo infectious-disease dataset (12,090 classes)
candidates.verdict: 12,090-class infectious-disease dataset; domain mismatch (excluded infectious diseases by scope).

candidates.name: uom190346a - Disease-Symptom Knowledge
candidates.verdict: Small community knowledge table (24 diseases); insufficient classes/samples.

candidates.name: DDXPlus (marked not-acquired by scope)
candidates.verdict: Well-documented but explicitly synthetic patient generation; does not resolve synthetic-data concern.

candidates.name: MIMIC-SR-ICD11 (marked not-acquired by scope)
candidates.verdict: Best real-clinical provenance but requires PhysioNet credentialed access; per governance rules not bypassed; requires manual authorization before consideration.
